tags.name: Org level webhooks
tags.description: Webhooks enable you to integrate Ocrolus with your application ecosystem better. You can subscribe to Ocrolus events, send them to any external Business Process Management (BPM) or Customer Relationship Management (CRM) application, and notify different users. For example, a Document has finished verification, a file upload has failed, or statistical analysis on a Book is complete.

post.description:
Set up an org-level webhook for your organization so your application can receive and respond to Ocrolus events in real time. Use this endpoint to create or update the webhook configuration. Ocrolus then delivers event payloads to your application as they occur, allowing you to automate downstream workflows.

---
You can find a list of supported org-level event types and their sample notifications in the [Org-level webhook guide](doc:organization-level-webhook#available-events).

> 📘
> Your webhook integration should respond to incoming notifications with a status of `200 OK` to indicate that it's working properly.

This API configures the secret key for a specific org-level webhook. Use this endpoint to add a new secret or update an existing one. The secret is used to sign webhook payloads using HMAC SHA256, allowing you to verify that requests originate from Ocrolus.

post.description:
This API sends a test payload to your configured webhook endpoint using a provided event.

---
This endpoint requires users to provide an `event_uuid` for a notification event that you have configured a webhook for.

You can find configured notifications event and their uuids by using the [List events for Webhook endpoint](ref:list-events).

parameters.name: webhook_uuid
parameters.description: The unique identification code (UUID) of the webhook.

event_uuid.description: The unique universal identification code of the event that you would like to test for.

event_name.description: The name of the notification event delievered by Ocrolus.

severity.description: The configured importance level for this type of event.

notification_reason.description: A written explanation of the event that triggered the notification.

notification_type.description: Describes the type of notification the event triggered.

book_uuid.description: A unique identification code (uuid) of the <<glossary:Book>> from which the event was triggered from.
